name: drift
description: Finds which dependency updates break your code, proves it with evidence, and fixes them with the AI agent you already use.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Drift runs git commands and can invoke local AI agent binaries, so it requires a trusted workspace.

commands.title: Keep All Changes in This File
Undo All Changes in This File
Open Diff for a Changed File

drift.agent.preferred.markdownDescription:
Which AI agent fixes your code. Drift drives an agent **you already have** and never asks for an API key.

Set from the Drift panel: **+ → Model**. `auto` uses the best available.

Known ids: `copilot-lm`, `copilot-cloud`, `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `aider`, `opencode`, `ollama`, and `lm:<vendor>` for any other chat-model provider registered in your editor — Drift discovers those, so the list is not fixed.

drift.agent.models.markdownDescription:
The model chosen inside each subscription, keyed by agent id — for example `{ "claude": "opus" }`.

Set from the subscription buttons in the Drift panel. A subscription with no entry uses whatever model it picks by default.

enumDescriptions: Drift may edit your files through your AI agent
Drift only analyses and explains; it never edits
drift.session.mode.markdownDescription: Set from the picker in the Drift panel. **Ask** analyses and explains. **Agent** lets your AI agent edit code.

drift.agent.efforts.markdownDescription:
How hard each subscription's model is asked to think, keyed by agent id — for example `{ "claude": "xhigh" }`.

Set from the effort dial in the Drift panel, where each level carries the name its own vendor uses: Claude runs `low`–`high` and `xhigh` (**Ultracode**), Codex runs `low`–`high` and `xhigh` (**Extra High**). Agents whose API has no reasoning budget — the in-editor Copilot models, Ollama — have no dial.

This only changes the reasoning spent on each fix. It never changes which dependencies Drift checks or which fixes it attempts — see `#drift.analysis.includeDev#` and `#drift.analysis.includePatch#` for that.

drift.session.effort.markdownDeprecationMessage:
Replaced by `#drift.agent.efforts#`, which is set per subscription and carries each vendor's own names for its stops.

Effort no longer changes what Drift analyses — it never should have. Use `#drift.analysis.includeDev#` and `#drift.analysis.includePatch#` for that. An existing value here is still honoured as the starting position of every agent's dial.

enumDescriptions: Ask in the panel before editing each group of files
Edit files, then wait for you to keep or undo each change
Edit files and commit each group without stopping
drift.session.permission.markdownDescription:
Set from the picker in the Drift panel. How much your AI agent may do unsupervised.

On the default, **Edit, then review**, nothing is ever committed until you keep it.

drift.agent.copilotModelFamily.markdownDescription: Optional model family for the in-editor Copilot agent (for example `gpt-4o`). Leave blank to let VS Code choose.

drift.agent.ollamaHost.description: Where your Ollama server is listening.

drift.agent.ollamaModel.description: Which Ollama model to use. A coding-tuned model works far better here than a general one.

drift.agent.timeoutSeconds.description: How long to let an agent work on a single commit before giving up.

drift.analysis.runOnStartup.markdownDescription: Check for breaking changes when a folder opens. Drift stays silent unless it finds something.

drift.analysis.includePatch.markdownDescription: Analyse patch bumps too. Breakage there is usually accidental, but it does happen — around 5% of npm packages have been broken by a minor or patch release.

drift.analysis.includeDev.description: Analyse dev dependencies. They rarely break production code paths.

drift.analysis.concurrency.markdownDescription: How many packages to check at once. Checking one is almost entirely waiting on the network, so raising this shortens a scan roughly in proportion — up to the point where the GitHub API starts rate-limiting, which turns evidence into 'could not check'.

drift.analysis.includeTransitive.description: Analyse lockfile-only changes you did not ask for. Noisy, and rarely actionable.

drift.analysis.ignore.markdownDescription: Package name patterns to never analyse, for example `@types/*`. Added to any `ignore` list in `.github/drift.yml`.

drift.ui.showInlineDiagnostics.markdownDescription: Flag affected lines in the editor and the Problems panel. Severity follows Drift's confidence: high is an error, low is information.

drift.fix.customInstructions.markdownDescription:
Repository conventions passed to every agent. The highest-leverage setting for output quality.

For example: *"This repo uses Vitest, not Jest. Prefer named exports. All HTTP goes through src/lib/http.ts."*

drift.git.branchPrefix.markdownDescription:
Prefix for branches Drift creates, so a team can keep its own naming convention — `drift` gives `drift/upgrade-react-19.2.0`.

Drift never commits without asking, never force-pushes, never rewrites history, and never commits a file an upgrade did not change.

drift.logLevel.description: How much Drift writes to its output channel.

scripts.package: npm run typecheck && npm run build && npx --yes @vscode/vsce package --no-dependencies --out drift.vsix && code --install-extension ./drift.vsix --force
